sections.title: The Trauma Spectrum and Its Treatment: The PRISM Meta-Model
sections.description: Research findings document that trauma is a ubiquitous human experience with many types and variations. It is often a highly personalized exposure or experience (individual, group, and collective) that has a wide range of pycho-social and neuro-physiological consequences. Both the types of trauma and types of response make up the trauma spectrum. This course will introduce this spectrum and contemporary trauma theory and findings. Due to the large number of traumatized individuals who seek services for current and past symptoms, social workers and other mental health (and medical) professionals can expect to treat a variety of traumatized clients over the course of their careers. Course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

sections.title: Trauma Interventions
sections.description: Given the prevalence of trauma and its long-lasting effects, professionals in social work and behavioral health frequently encounter individuals seeking support for trauma-related challenges. This course focuses on equipping practitioners with an advanced understanding of trauma-informed assessment, treatment interventions, and resilience-based services.  Students will explore the complexities of trauma treatment, including managing challenges and crises, addressing common countertransference and reenactment dynamics, understanding the impact of vicarious traumatization, and fostering post-traumatic growth in both clients and practitioners.  The course will also emphasize the importance of considering the client’s context, intersectionality, and cultural background, as well as addressing social justice issues related to trauma causation, consequences, and healing.  The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.
